reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let J be finite with decidable equality, Omega a measurable space with finite measure mu, F a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, T>0, and B an R^J-valued standard Brownian motion with F. A vector standard Brownian motion with filtration F here starts at zero for every sample, has jointly independent increments over each finite family of disjoint half-open intervals, has centered Gaussian increment projections with variance (t-s)*||ell||^2 for every continuous linear functional ell and s<t, has almost surely continuous paths, is strongly F-adapted, and has each increment from s to t independent of F_s when s<=t. Usual conditions mean every null subset of Omega belongs to every F_t, and F is right-continuous. Write lambda_H for real Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,H] and transported to NNReal. A progressive L2 integrand on horizon H is a real strongly F-progressive process belonging to L2(mu product lambda_H), after ordering its arguments as (omega,t). Write I^H_j(h)(t) for its specified completed Ito integral against the coordinate B_j(t,omega) of B. This is the canonical elementary-approximation path limit, patched to zero on its exceptional null set and held constant after H. For each j in J let eta_j be a progressive L2 integrand on [0,T]. Let tau:Omega->NNReal be a stopping time for F (through its inclusion in WithTop NNReal), with tau(omega)<=T for every omega. Let A:NNReal x Omega->R have, for every t<=T, an mu-almost-everywhere strongly measurable slice A(t,.), and have paths continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T] for mu-almost every omega. Define
X(t,omega)=A(t,omega)+sum_j I^T_j(eta_j)(min(tau(omega),t),omega).
For n in N set t_i^n=i*T/2^n. Then sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1}(X(t_{i+1}^n,omega)-X(t_i^n,omega))^2 converges in mu-measure, as n tends to infinity, to sum_j integral_{[0,T] intersect [0,tau(omega)]} eta_j(s,omega)^2 ds. Only the Ito-integral part of X is stopped; A is evaluated at the unstopped time t. No adaptedness assumption on A is made.
objects: Finite J,Omega,mu,F,T,B, progressive L2 eta_j, bounded stopping time tau, continuous bounded-variation term A, stopped-noise process X, dyadic grids, quadratic-sum limit.
domains: Time NNReal; tau finite NNReal-valued; real process A,X; B in EuclideanSpace R J; finite mu.
quantifiers: For all such data including tau pointwise bounded by T and A satisfying the slice/path conditions, the dyadic sequence converges in mu-measure to the given random energy.
assumptions: T>0; standard vector Brownian with usual filtration; eta_j progressive L2; tau stopping time and tau<=T for every omega; A_t a.e. strongly measurable for each t<=T; a.e. A-path continuous and bounded variation on [0,T].
conclusion: Quadratic sums of A plus stopped stochastic integral converge in measure to the sum of integrated squared coefficients up to tau.
scopes: Dyadic partitions cover the entire fixed [0,T]; noise evaluated at min(tau,t), A not stopped. Limit is an omega-dependent path integral restricted by s<=tau(omega). Convergence is in measure, not a.s. or Lp. A-path event is uniform over [0,T], slice measurability is separately quantified per time.
constant_dependencies: No numeric bound or convergence rate. tau may depend on omega and filtration; its upper bound is the fixed T. eta,A and all stochastic data determine the limit sequence.
